The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
1,\,11,\,121,\,1\,331,\,…
$$

form a geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=11:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =11 \\  & =\frac{11}{1} \\  & =\frac{121}{11} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our geometric sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1}=1\cdot {11}^{n-1}={11}^{n-1}.
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
A={{11}^{n-1}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{11}^{N-1} & =214\,358\,881 \\ N-1 & ={log}_{11}⁡(214\,358\,881) \\ N-1 & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(214\,358\,881)}{{log}_{10}⁡(11)} \\ N-1 & =8 \\ N & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={{11}^{n-1}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 9}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $9$ elements, we must have $|A|=9.$
